scenario.title: Where Yoke runs and who can reach it
situations: A local user mentions another computer
Joining an existing team or hosted organization
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Do prompts distinguish connection reachability, membership and machine permission?
Do server, hosted and local branches each name the next reachable action?

lessons.title: Local, team server or hosted
lessons.when: Choosing a destination; later mentions of another machine
lessons.need: Local means reachable on this machine only. Shared access requires an appropriate server/hosted setup; a second checkout is not a second connection.
lessons.surface: Installer choice, yoke status and modes guide
lessons.gap: The modes exist. FIRST-USER 3 adds the missing explanation and recovery; JOURNEYS extends when it is raised.

lessons.title: Account, organization and machine approval
lessons.when: Connecting to the selected control plane
lessons.need: Sign-in, organization membership and authority to use a machine are distinct. The human completes required authorization; the agent needs pending/success/failure state.
lessons.surface: Hosted/team authorization and human approval UI
lessons.gap: The standalone hosted beta and organization-creation redesign is implemented in a candidate: plain titles, named invitation failures, settled URL/Subscription rows and one creation indicator. Its quiet wait line changes after 45 seconds to teach resuming after a closed tab. Candidate screenshots do not replace production captures, exact deployed proof or timed real stage founding acceptance. Shared machine approval remains separate unfinished work. Local/self-hosted modes do not use the standalone hosted screens.
lessons.review: Candidate fixture screenshots and focused checks are recorded separately from pending CI retention, deployed screen proof and real stage acceptance. FIRST-USER 27 covers both standalone hosted setup and shared machine approval; 33 spans membership and machine access across modes.
